summary: Iteration 5 fully verified — pagination, server-side search, unread/mark-read, fresh_start, and 3-layer UIDNEXT fallback all work as specified. 41/41 pytest cases pass (18 new + 23 regression). Frontend Inbox pagination + debounced search + load-more + channel counts all render correctly end-to-end on kamal's account.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py list_conversations line 927 reads `limit = min(max(limit, 200), 200)` when q is set — this is equivalent to `limit = 200` (the min/max pair cancels out). Consider simplifying to `limit = 200` for readability; functionally correct today but easy to misread in review.

list_conversations.unread_total is computed with `dict(mongo_q, unread=True)` which overrides any existing `unread` key if a caller ever passed one. Today no caller does, but if an `unread=` filter is added later the count will silently diverge. Consider renaming local to `unread_filter` and using `{**mongo_q, 'unread': True}` for explicit intent.

email_routes.py line 598 uses `getattr(req, 'fresh_start', False)` after the model explicitly defines `fresh_start: Optional[bool] = False`. The getattr is redundant here — `req.fresh_start` is always defined. Safe, but deletes the extra defensive shim.

Inbox.jsx channel-count refresh fires 6 parallel requests every time the status filter changes — fine today, but the responses are thrown away if the component unmounts mid-flight (no AbortController). Could fire stale state updates in dev strict-mode. Low priority.

Inbox.jsx mark-read calls api.post(`/conversations/${id}/read`) inside openThread — this fires for EVERY open even if the thread was already read. Cheap (single indexed update), but adds unnecessary writes. Gate behind `if (data?.conversation?.unread)` check which is already done for the local list update but NOT for the API call.
